summary: Active II has an overt affected object in 78/73 and absolute soiling in Hors 2/99–103. taḥta makes bodily waste plausible, but does not by itself establish a separate defecation meaning.
Detransitive examples span becoming dirty and a resultant dirty condition. Part. Pass. occurs literally with dishes, a muddy filly and dirty things, and evaluatively in insults.
82/56 adds figurative speech/content dirt as 1b; the repeated garwono mlawto insults do not independently demonstrate obscene language.
mlawto in 78/73 is already inside a finite Preterit quotation, but was not filed in its own Part. Pass. box. It is added there once, with the finite token's decision remaining no_add.

The Nomen Actionis heading and lewoto belong to active nominal material; its inherited Detransitive placement is repaired explicitly. The revised layout displays the canonical target Nomen Actionis in the active section; this is a structural move, not a change of lexical meaning.
The supplied German at 73/165 is corrupt ('ihr hart', 'sehr nutz'). Existing English quotation is retained; no reconstructed German text added.

All four tokens reviewed. Three literal examples fill active or Detransitive Infectum cells left thin after round 1; one figurative state example extends its Detransitive 1b rather than repeating that sense proposal.

Animal soiling has an external affected place; milawto has the country as affected subject and coordinates with stinking/deterioration. In the shoe-removal verse, d lə favors a prospective active Infectum, despite mlawti being compatible elsewhere with other forms.
Round 1's explicit Detransitive senses and active Nomen Actionis refiling are comparison-baseline changes, not repeated round 2 corrections.
Printed mlawatto yo is retained, including its agreement question. Supplied machine English is quoted as tangled; it is not silently replaced with legally compromised.
